chapters.chapter: 11.1 Surface Area of a Right Circular Cone
chapters.summary: This section explains how a cone can be generated by rotating a right triangle around one of its perpendicular sides. The cone has a circular base of radius r, height h, and slant height l, where l = √(h² + r²). The curved surface of a cone can be 'opened' into a sector of a circle. Using this idea, the curved surface area (CSA) is derived as πrl. Adding the area of the base (πr²) gives the total surface area (TSA) = πr(l + r). Worked examples include finding CSA and TSA given radius and slant height, computing slant height from radius and height, and real-life applications such as counting grains on a corn cob.
formulas: Total Surface Area: TSA = πr(l + r)

chapters.summary: Real-world applications include calculating metal sheet needed to make cones, finding paint required to cover conical surfaces, modeling decorative items, designing roofs, and estimating material for food packaging.
Key ideas include how cones are formed, how slant height is computed, and how surface areas are derived from unfolding (net diagrams). Exercises reinforce geometric reasoning and formula application.
